title: Understand GPIO on Cortex-M based microcontrollers
shortdesc: General-purpose input/output (GPIO) peripherals allow software to monitor and control physical pins on a microcontroller.

conbody.p: A microcontroller can contain an Arm Cortex-M processor alongside memory and peripherals. GPIO is typically one of those peripherals, not a feature of the processor core itself.

li.p: Input: Software reads a pin state, such as whether a button is pressed.
Output: Software sets a pin state, such as driving a connected indicator LED, subject to the board's electrical design.

section.title: Device-specific configuration
section.p: The available pins, GPIO registers, pin multiplexing, electrical limits, and configuration procedure depend on the microcontroller and board. Before following a configuration procedure, consult the device reference manual and board documentation.

Some devices provide a software driver interface for GPIO. The Arm CMSIS-Driver GPIO interface, when implemented for the device, defines operations for pin configuration, output control, and input reading.
